GATE EE 2027 — Predicted Paper (practice)

65 questions · 100 marks · 3 hours — same pattern as GATE EE 2026: General Aptitude 10 questions (15 marks), Engineering Mathematics ≈ 13 marks, Electrical Engineering ≈ 72 marks; MCQ, MSQ and NAT. Built from the trend of all 1670 GATE EE questions of 20 years (2007–2026).

Read this first. These are original practice questions written on the concepts most likely to be asked — they are not the actual GATE 2027 questions (nobody can know those in advance). Every answer is worked out and the numericals are checked by computer. Use the paper under exam conditions, then check the key and the worked solutions; each solution says why that concept was predicted.

How to use

1. Part B: attempt all 65 in 3 hours (no peeking).

2. Part C: mark with the answer key (MCQ wrong: −⅓ for 1-mark, −⅔ for 2-mark; MSQ and NAT: no negative marks).

3. Part D: read the worked solution of every question you missed or guessed, then revise that row in the Study Book.

What 2026 changed: more matrix theory (8 marks: rank, orthogonal and skew-symmetric matrices), more circuit theorems (7 marks), protection relays in the admittance plane, phase-shifting transformers in Y-bus, and power-electronics device behaviour (diode loss, turn-off overshoot). The predicted paper keeps the 2016– 2026 subject balance, puts the always-asked concepts in, and adds the due ones (Routh–Hurwitz, steady-state error, synchronous motor excitation, single-phase full converter, DC motor speed, Newton–Raphson).
